items.text: Prografen PLA Graphene Light is an ideal choice for designers, hobbyists and engineers who need a material with improved performance that is easy to print, without requiring advanced printer settings.
Enriching PLA with graphene makes this filament well-suited for a wide range of demanding applications.
good alternative for styrene-based materials
functional prototyping
concept and demo prototyping of designed finished and semi-finished products
industrial design
parts that require high impact strength
This is a high molecular weight biopolymer that processes easily on conventional FDM/FDM 3D printer.

It contains approximately 0.5% edge-functionalized graphene flakes (EFG), which enhances the mechanical properties of the filament compared to standard PLA, while maintaining all the advantages of this popular material.
The small amount of graphene increases strength, flexibility and wear resistance, making this filament more durable than traditional PLA.
The material also exhibits good thermal conductivity, which can speed up the printing process while ensuring dimensional accuracy.

items.text: The filament is designed for precise detail printing at ultra-high speeds without the risk of defects or stringing.
Prografen PLA Graphene Strong excels in projects requiring high-quality finishes, strength and precision, such as functional prototypes or spare parts.
With the addition of graphene, the filament is resistant to abrasion, strong and lightweight, making it an ideal choice for technical and industrial applications.

Graphene doping also increases the stiffness of the material by over 15% compared to pure polymer.

PLA PROGRAFEN GRAPHENE STRONG is easily processed on FDM/FFF 3D printers.
It contains 5% edge-functionalized graphene flakes (EFG), which gives it exceptional mechanical strength, abrasion resistance and flexibility.
Prografen PLA Graphene Strong can be printed at ultra-high speeds exceeding 1000 mm/s, which is unattainable for other materials currently available on the market.

Less shrinkage compared to pure PLA.
Its very high melt flow rate (MFR – 44 g/10min) and low shrinkage allow for excellent dimensional stability of the prints.
PLA with the addition of graphene allows for the production of precise details at ultra-high printing speeds without issues with voids or stringing.
In addition, the material does not require special nozzles or climate chambers.
Can be extruded with standard nozzles without the risk of excessive wear unlike carbon fibre materials.

Of the solvents studied, chloroform is the best solvent for quickly preparing 10 % wt/vol solutions of all Ingeo grades and morphologies; 4032D pellets and injection-moulded bars were readily transformed to 10 % wt/vol solutions in chloroform in 2-4 hours at room temperature
items.conditions: 10 % wt/vol mixture, shaken at 175 rpm at room temperature; some samples stirred at 65 °C
items.note: Study grades: 4060D (12 % D, amorphous), 2003D (4.5 % D) and 4032D (1.6 % D, crystallisable) as pellets and injection-moulded bars; no filament grade was tested. A printed part is largely amorphous, so the amorphous-bar results are the nearer case. The reference reports dissolution; the verdict word "soluble" is reserved for water, so dissolution in an organic solvent is recorded as not-resistant.

items.text: In-line drying is required. A moisture content of less than 0.025 % (250 ppm) is recommended to prevent viscosity degradation. Typical drying conditions are 4 hours at 80 °C (175 °F) to a dew point of -40 °C (-40 °F).
items.note: A processing threshold (hydrolytic loss of melt viscosity), not an equilibrium water uptake; the percentage in the finding is the recommended maximum before melting.
